summary: This note covers how Yugoslavia and its successor states participated in the Olympic Games after the country's breakup. The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, formed by Montenegro and Serbia, competed as Independent Olympic Participants at the 1992 Summer Olympics due to a UN ban and was barred from the 1994 Winter Olympics. Successor nations then began competing independently, with all six former socialist republics participating separately by 2008 and Kosovo debuting at the 2016 Summer Olympics.
one_line: Overview of Yugoslavia's Olympic participation after 1992 and how its successor states, including Kosovo, competed independently.
key_facts: The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was formed as a joint state by only Montenegro and Serbia after the breakup of Yugoslavia.
The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia existed from 1992 to 2002.
Due to a UN ban, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was allowed to compete as Independent Olympic Participants at the 1992 Summer Olympics.
The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia was not allowed to compete at the 1994 Winter Olympics.
Croatia and Slovenia began competing as independent teams at the Olympics starting at the 1992 Winter Games.
Bosnia and Herzegovina began competing as an independent team at the 1992 Summer Games.
As of the 2008 Summer Olympics, all six successor nations, former socialist republics, had participated independently.
Kosovo, a former autonomous province, made its Olympic debut as an independent national team at the 2016 Summer Olympics.
